title: The 'Poltergeist' Curse: Every Death and Accident Explained
excerpt: Four Poltergeist actors died within six years of the 1982 film. The deaths, real skeletons and on-set accidents behind the Poltergeist curse, explained.
content:
Four actors from the Poltergeist films died within six years of the first movie’s release in 1982, and those deaths are the basis of what fans call the Poltergeist curse. Two of the four were young and their deaths came without warning: Dominique Dunne was killed at 22, and Heather O’Rourke died at 12. The legend grew again in 2002, when JoBeth Williams said on VH1 that the skeletons in the first film’s swimming pool scene were real human remains. The people who made the films say there is no curse.

Dominique Dunne Was Killed Five Months After the First Film Opened

Poltergeist opened in June 1982 with Dunne as Dana, the oldest of the three Freeling children. On October 30 of that year, her ex-boyfriend John Thomas Sweeney strangled her in the driveway of her West Hollywood home. She never regained consciousness and died on November 4, 1982, nineteen days before her 23rd birthday.

A jury acquitted Sweeney of second-degree murder in September 1983 and convicted him of voluntary manslaughter. He was sentenced to six and a half years and served less than four.

Julian Beck Died Before ‘Poltergeist II’ Reached Theaters

Julian Beck played Kane, the preacher who leads the spirits in Poltergeist II: The Other Side. Beck had been diagnosed with stomach cancer in 1983. He died on September 14, 1985, at age 60, and the sequel opened in May 1986.

Will Sampson Died a Year After the Sequel

Will Sampson, known for One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest, played the medicine man Taylor in Poltergeist II. He received a heart-lung transplant in April 1987 and died on June 3, 1987, at age 53, of kidney failure and infection after the surgery.

Heather O’Rourke Died at 12, Before ‘Poltergeist III’ Was Released

O’Rourke played Carol Anne Freeling in all three films. In 1987 doctors diagnosed her with Crohn’s disease, which later proved to be a misdiagnosis. She became ill on January 31, 1988, and died the next day, February 1, at Children’s Hospital in San Diego during surgery for a bowel obstruction. The cause was septic shock brought on by a congenital narrowing of the intestine.

Poltergeist III, which also starred Tom Skerritt and Nancy Allen, had finished principal photography in Chicago in June 1987. O’Rourke died before a planned reshoot of the ending, which was completed with a stand-in, and the film opened on June 10, 1988. Director Gary Sherman has said he wanted to shelve the film after she died and that MGM refused.

The Skeletons in the Pool Scene Were Real

Near the end of the first film, Diane Freeling, played by Williams, falls into the muddy pit dug for the family’s swimming pool, and skeletons rise out of the water around her. Makeup effects artist Craig Reardon confirmed under oath that they were real. In a deposition taken in late 1982 for a lawsuit over the film’s screenplay, he said, “I acquired a number of actual biological surgical skeletons.”

Williams has said she did not know while filming. “I always assumed that the skeletons were made by the prop department,” she told Vanity Fair in 2022, and she learned otherwise a few years later from someone who had worked on the film. Fans who believe in the curse point to the scene as its cause, because the plot of Poltergeist is about a house built over a cemetery whose bodies were never moved.

Will Sampson Performed a Ceremony on the ‘Poltergeist II’ Set

Williams has also said the unease over the skeletons carried over to the sequel, and that Sampson performed what she called an exorcism on the Poltergeist II set after filming wrapped one night.

A Clown Prop Caught Oliver Robins by the Neck

Oliver Robins played Robbie, the Freelings’ son, who is dragged under his bed by a toy clown in the first film. Robins told Icons of Fright that while he was under the bed, the mechanism that moved the clown’s arm tightened on him. “That contraption got caught around my neck,” he said. By his account, Steven Spielberg saw it on a monitor and pulled him free. The film was rated PG and is on our list of family-friendly horror movies.

A Fire Injured Three People on ‘Poltergeist III’

During the Chicago shoot in 1987, an explosion staged for a scene in a snow-covered parking garage set fire to the set. A maintenance worker and two firefighters were injured, and the damage was estimated at $250,000.

Later Events Fans Add to the List

Two events from after the trilogy are often added. Richard Lawson, who played Ryan on the parapsychology team in the first film, survived the crash of USAir Flight 405 at LaGuardia Airport on March 22, 1992, which killed 27 of the 51 people aboard. Lou Perryman, who had a small part as Pugsley in the first film, was killed in his home in 2009 by a man who pleaded guilty and received a life sentence.

The Cast and Crew Say There Is No Curse

Robins, the only one of the three Freeling children still living, rejects the idea. “I hope there isn’t a curse, because I’m still around,” he told Yahoo Entertainment in 2022, adding that each of the deaths has an explanation.

Reardon has objected to the link drawn between the skeletons and the deaths. Jay Cheel, who directed the 2020 Shudder series Cursed Films, told Den of Geek that Reardon “takes extreme personal offense” at the suggestion. In the same series, Sherman called the legend a way to avoid dealing with what happened to O’Rourke and Dunne.

O’Rourke’s family addressed the rumors in She Was Here, a documentary about her life released in February 2026. In the film, according to People, her sister Tammy O’Rourke says the comments people post about Heather’s death are “just so hurtful.” Craig T. Nelson and Williams, who played the Freeling parents, both appear in the documentary.
